phase0Attempt2.result: artifact-integrity-powershell, artifact-integrity-node and bootstrap-core PASS; git-baseline FAIL with a NativeCommandError (error: No such remote 'origin') at scripts/init-private-git.ps1; nothing was pushed
phase0Attempt2.superseded: the ca21e83 release is superseded by the release built from this package

PHASE0-F4.cause: init-private-git.ps1 runs under ErrorActionPreference=Stop and probed the origin remote with a redirected native command (git remote get-url origin 2>$null); on a fresh repository git writes 'No such remote' to stderr and Windows PowerShell 5.1 turns that redirected stderr line into a terminating NativeCommandError, so the git-baseline step aborted before the remote was added. The gh repo view probe used the same pattern (inside try/catch, so it degraded to REMOTE_UNVERIFIED instead of aborting).
PHASE0-F4.fix: both probes run with a scoped ErrorActionPreference=Continue that is restored in finally, and their result is decided only by the exit code; the origin probe output (an existing remote URL, possibly with credentials) is discarded instead of written to the output; a failed gh probe throws inside the existing try and is classified REMOTE_UNVERIFIED.
PHASE0-F4.unchanged: ErrorActionPreference=Stop for the script, Git isolation (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM, core.hooksPath), the NOT_PRIVATE refusal, the unverified-remote refusal without -AllowUnverifiedRemote, the push exit check, the remote SHA verification and REMOTE_STATUS.json
PHASE0-F4.edgeCase: a gh probe that exits non-zero without writing stderr was previously parsed as empty output and classified NOT_PRIVATE (refuse); it is now REMOTE_UNVERIFIED, which still refuses the push unless the operator passes -AllowUnverifiedRemote after manual privacy verification (the documented meaning of that override).
